extracted.intended_audience: social scientists, researchers, and members of the public interested in open-access preprint repositories
extracted.subtask_description: Summarize the purpose, scope, and submission/functional features of the SocArXiv preprint repository for the social sciences. Focuses on what the platform accepts, its access model, and its support for openness and post-publication review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open-archive model (ArXiv model)
rubrics_metrics.description: SocArXiv "is an online paper server for the social sciences" and "an open archive based on the ArXiv preprint server model used for the natural sciences, mathematics, and computer science."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied expectation that the server follows an arXiv-style open-archive approach: publicly accessible uploads of manuscripts without (initial) journal gatekeeping. The page frames SocArXiv as a discipline-specific analogue to arXiv.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free, non-profit, open-access platform
rubrics_metrics.description: The site describes itself as "an open archive of the social sciences, [which] provides a free, non-profit, open access platform for social scientists..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission and access are intended to be cost-free and non-commercial; emphasis on removal of paywalls and commercialization barriers for access to scholarship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted submission formats: working papers, preprints, and postprints
rubrics_metrics.description: Format coverage: "preprints, postprints, working papers" and the site allows social scientists to "upload working papers, preprints, and published papers."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may deposit manuscripts at multiple stages (preprint, postprint, published version). The listing defines what content types the repository accepts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Option to link data and code
rubrics_metrics.description: The platform provides authors "the option to link data and code."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages reproducibility and transparency by allowing (and implying encouragement of) connections between papers and their underlying data/code artifacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage linking and sharing of data and code (openness principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: SocArXiv was created to "encourage[] linking and sharing data and code, that serves its research to an open metadata system, and that provides the foundation for a post-publication review system."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repository's purpose includes active promotion of open-science practices (sharing data/code, exposing metadata) as a quality/ethical norm for submissions and dissemination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serve research to an open metadata system (interoperability)
rubrics_metrics.description: One stated aim is that SocArXiv "serves its research to an open metadata system."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied requirement/expectation that repository records be machine-readable/interoperable and that metadata be openly exposed to enable discovery and reuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for post-publication peer review / hosting peer reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: The database was launched ... to provide "the foundation for a post-publication review system." Philip N. Cohen has called for "a central repository for peer-reviews of papers even when the reviews lead to the paper being declined for publication."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates that SocArXiv aims to enable or host post-publication review outputs (reviews, commentary) to increase transparency of peer review and preserve review artifacts irrespective of journal decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disciplinary coverage: social sciences, education, and law
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage: "Social sciences, education, law." The site hosts papers in the areas of education and law in addition to social sciences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the scope of acceptable subject areas for deposits and for the repository's community focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform and institutional hosting (built on OSF; Univ. of Maryland stewardship)
rubrics_metrics.description: SocArXiv "was built of the Open Science Framework platform, initially as a program of the University of Maryland." In 2021, the University of Maryland Libraries became the institutional home of SocArXiv.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical/administrative details that affect governance, preservation, and platform capabilities: being built on OSF implies certain features (integration with OSF tools, metadata practices) and institutional stewardship implies longevity/trustworthiness considerations.
